title: North Programme — Biblical Cross-Reference Index
method: Intertextual reference only. These passages are preserved with their historical and literary context; they are not treated as proof that Tim Dooley is a biblical figure or that the modern programme is biblically ordained.

references.key: mount of assembly / far north / Most High / throne
Gog / far north / nations / divine judgement
king of the north / king of the south
throne / river / tree of life / renewal

required_context_notes.psalm48: Psalm 48 identifies Zion with the sides of the north and calls it the city of the great King; the project may use this as symbolic vocabulary but should not erase the psalm's Zion/Jerusalem context.
required_context_notes.isaiah14: Isaiah 14 is a taunt against the king of Babylon. The 'mount of assembly' and 'sides/far north' language is important for comparative symbolism but cannot simply be reassigned to Tim.
required_context_notes.ezekiel38: Ezekiel 38 describes Gog, Magog and nations associated with the far north. The identity of these places is debated and should not be reduced to a modern geopolitical prediction.
required_context_notes.daniel11: Daniel 11's kings of the north and south belong to a specific historical-prophetic framework. The language can inform a study of North/South geopolitical symbolism without proving the modern programme.
required_context_notes.revelation: Revelation's throne and Tree of Life imagery provides a strong thematic connection to the user's mythic framework, but the text's theological context remains primary.
